text:
maya: quick q — can we allow short ~200 req/sec spikes per org for up to 5s without penalizing downstream?
kevin: context? are these API keys hitting streaming endpoints or embedding batch jobs?
maya: mostly streaming chat from web clients during reconnects. steady-state is ~10 rps/org but gauntlet spike to 300 for a few seconds when network flaps.
sarah: token-bucket seems fine: low refill_rate = steady, capacity = burst_size. question is how to pick capacity to avoid backlog.
rohit: leaky-bucket (fixed drain) is equivalent but harder to map to UX. token bucket easier to reason with: tokens refill at R tokens/sec, capacity C tokens. allow burst=C.
kevin: agrees. proposed defaults: R = org_quota_per_sec, C = max(10*R, 200). but that may be too permissive for small orgs.
maya: suggest dynamic C = min(200, max(20, 5*R)). gives headroom for small orgs.
ops-bot: metric: rate_limited_requests, rate_limited_reason, dropped_spike_count.
sarah: also need smoothing for multi-key customers: per-org should aggregate across keys. risk: one key can hoard tokens if we keep per-key buckets.
rohit: implement hierarchy: per-key bucket with token share from org bucket. algorithm: try consume from key bucket then fallback to org bucket.
kevin: code sample for config:
```
rate_limit:
  refill_per_sec: 10
  burst_capacity: 50
  short_spike_ttl_sec: 5
  enforcement: token_bucket
```
maya: can we special-case streaming start/finish? e.g., allow small extra tokens for "open" events to avoid UI flapping.
sarah: telemetry: capture token_leakback metric for when we force-return tokens. also histograms of latency when throttled.
kevin: rollout plan: feature-flag in API layer, default off, 1% orgs, monitor rate_limited_requests and 95th latency, then 10%, 50%...
maya: UI: in Console show "burst profile" with slider: conservative, balanced, aggressive and show estimated burst seconds at current R.
rohit: operational concern: spikes can be replayed from retrying clients -> need to detect retry storm patterns and temporarily tighten burst to 1s.
maya: perf: implementing in rust worker, will be O(1) per request, state in etcd for persistence? prefer in-memory with periodic snapshot to avoid latency.
sarah: add log line when quota refill falls behind: "quota_backpressure org=... gap=...".
kevin: agree. Action items: rohit to implement hierarchical buckets prototype (rohit), sarah to add telemetry and alerts, maya to mock console UI, kevin to own rollout plan.
maya: thanks — putting PR up later today and will ping this thread. :thumbsup:
